They also cover cross-document view transitions and the rules for reading custom clipboard formats, helping ensure those features behave consistently and respect origin-based restrictions.

features.summary: Firefox improves how session history interacts with the back-forward cache and restores pages, including avoiding restoration of `javascript:` URLs. It also fixes a same-origin check for saved `about:srcdoc` pages, so the Navigation API uses the embedded page’s inherited origin correctly.

patches.subject: Only send the page swap target entry to the process of the top document.

features.summary: The changes make navigation reporting more reliable: starting a download now triggers only one `navigate` event, and page-swap information is sent only to the process handling the top-level page. They also restore tests that pass on debug, optimized, and AddressSanitizer builds, while limiting skips to configurations where tests still fail—improving coverage across Firefox’s build types.

patches.subject: Hold strong reference to ImageListener and requests during OnStartRequest

patches.author: Bas Schouten
patches.subject: Ensure that native-anonymous content doesn't use a cached container timing root.

features.summary: Crash tests now cover fixes for image loading and page-layout timing: Firefox keeps the image-loading resources alive while a request starts and avoids reusing a stale timing context for browser-managed content. This helps prevent crashes in these less common loading and layout situations.

features.label: Build

patches.author: Lars Eggert
patches.subject: Remove dead socket process code from NetworkConnectivityService and unused ALLOW_IN_SOCKET_PROCESS entries.

features.summary: Removed obsolete code and permissions for the network socket process, simplifying Firefox’s build and trimming support for a process that is no longer used.

features.label: HTML elements tests

patches.author: Keith Cirkel
patches.subject: Test setting form controls after parse

features.summary: Added a test for changing form controls after the page has been parsed. This helps catch cases where controls don’t correctly reflect updates made after they first appear.

features.label: HTML parser (legacy)

patches.author: Henri Sivonen
patches.subject: Stop generating speculative loads inside the template element.

features.summary: Firefox no longer starts speculative resource loads while parsing content inside an HTML `template` element. Because template contents are inert until used, this avoids unnecessary downloads and work, improving efficiency without changing the template’s intended behavior.

features.label: Jsactor

patches.author: Nika Layzell
patches.subject: Don't crash late during shutdown in JSActor code.

features.summary: A shutdown fix prevents Firefox from crashing when JavaScript actor activity finishes late in the browser’s closing process. This is an internal reliability improvement, with no intended change to normal browsing behavior.

features.label: Reftests

patches.author: Jamie Nicol
patches.subject: Stop skipping remaining reftests for Android isolated process.

features.summary: Updated Android reftests—tests that compare rendered pages against expected results—so one isolated-process failure no longer causes the remaining tests to be skipped. This lets more of the suite run and can reveal additional rendering problems.

features.label: Rust

patches.author: Keith Cirkel
patches.subject: Reshuffle bits so FULLSCREEN_KEYBOARD_LOCK doesn't conflict with HEADING_LEVEL_BITS

features.summary: This Rust change rearranges internal bit assignments so the fullscreen keyboard-lock setting no longer overlaps with heading-level bits. It is an internal correctness fix, with no intended visible change for users.

features.summary: The WebIDL binding tests add coverage for `Set`- and `Map`-like web interfaces backed directly by browser storage. This checks that APIs using these collection patterns behave correctly and consistently for websites.
